key_evidence_spans: A 36-year-old woman presented with sudden-onset, sharp upper abdominal pain rated 9/10
The pain was minimally relieved by oxycodone and worsened with oral intake
Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT demonstrated a cluster of small-bowel loops in the left upper quadrant, positioned anterior to the splenic flexure
The central mesenteric vessels exhibited a spiral (whirl) pattern, with congestion of mesenteric fat and stretching and convergence of vessels
The patient had undergone Roux-en-Y gastric bypass, which can increase the risk of internal hernia and other complications
The patient's white-cell count was 10.5 × 10^9/L, which is slightly elevated
The patient's C-reactive protein was < 0.5 mg/L, which is within normal limits
The patient's lactate was 1 mmol/L, which is within normal limits
